problem: Prior open-vocabulary navigation methods (CoW, LM-Nav) use VLMs as critics disconnected from environment mapping, lacking spatial precision for goals like 'between the sofa and TV', cannot be shared across embodiments, and ignore non-visual modalities such as audio.
motivation: Humans build cognitive maps and integrate multiple senses to navigate and disambiguate goals (e.g. the table where a cough was heard). A unified spatial map that anchors pretrained multimodal features in 3D lets an LLM compose precise spatial and multimodal goals zero-shot, without training data.
key_idea: Fuse pretrained visual-language, audio-language and visual-localization features into a 3D reconstruction (VLMaps/AVLMaps), turn each modality's query into a heatmap, and let an LLM write code that composes heatmaps (element-wise product) for cross-modal goal disambiguation.
insight: Multiplying heatmaps with different decay rates (primary sharp, auxiliary broad) is a simple but effective way to disambiguate goals: adding object context to sound goals raises Recall@1 (<0.5m) from 26.05 (AudioCLIP alone) to 53.78, and adding the visual module raises visual-object recall from 7.55 to 62.26. Performance scales with the audio model (CLAP over AudioCLIP gives about +10 points on sound goals), but newer dense VLMs (OVSeg, SAM+CLIP) bring little or no gain, so the pixel-level feature quality is the bottleneck. Fine-tuned segmentation features (LSeg) fail at region concepts, motivating an added sparse CLIP topological map.
method: VLMap construction: LSeg pixel embeddings (in CLIP space) are back-projected using depth and odometry to a top-down grid and averaged per cell; querying uses CLIP text embeddings with argmax similarity for open-vocabulary segmentation.

Open-vocabulary obstacle maps: per-embodiment lists of obstacle categories select subsets of the segmentation masks (intersected with the height-filtered depth obstacle map), so a drone and a LoCoBot get different maps from the same VLMap.

LLM code-generation navigation: few-shot prompted text-davinci-003 writes Python calling primitives (move_to_left, move_in_between, turn, move_forward, get_major_map, get_map, etc.) that are executed with exec; spatial goals are computed as offsets or averages of landmark positions.

AVLMaps localization modules: (i) visual localization with NetVLAD + SuperPoint + SuperGLUE + PnP, (ii) 3D voxel object localization with LSeg/OpenSeg/OVSeg features, (iii) area localization with a sparse topological CLIP feature map, (iv) audio localization with silence-segmented AudioCLIP/CLAP embeddings tied to odometry. Each returns a 3D heatmap with linear distance decay.

Cross-modal reasoning: heatmaps from different modalities are fused by element-wise multiplication, assuming conditional independence; the primary target uses a high decay rate (0.1) and auxiliary constraints a low rate (0.01); argmax gives the goal.
Execution: move_to projects the 3D goal to a 2D grid, plans a path, and converts it to low-level actions (turn 5°, forward 0.25 m) using the ROS navigation stack.
Real-world audio handling: a noise gate (attack, hold, release) plus silence segmentation preprocess audio recorded with background noise.

numbers_note: All benchmarks are custom (no standard benchmark such as R2R); splits are labelled 'val' as a placeholder since none is official. Real-world results are reported only as counts in text (20 tasks 50% overall; 6/10 multimodal spatial goals; tabletop 100% visual and sound, 9/13 object, 9/10 ambiguous).
results: VLMaps reaches 62/33/14/10% SR for 1-4 consecutive spatial subgoals versus CoW 33/5/0/0 and LM-Nav 5/5/0/0 (GT map 76/48/33/29). AVLMaps reaches 77.5% independent sound-goal SR and cross-modal disambiguation improves recall substantially (object-sound Recall@1 <0.5m 53.78 vs 26.05 for AudioCLIP alone), with ambiguous-goal SR 46.2% sound and 55.5% object versus 22.0% and 53.4% for the VLMaps+wav2clip multimodal baseline.
limitations: Requires offline pre-exploration mapping and monaural audio; cannot react to transient sounds or localize sound sources (sound is only tied to robot pose).
Cannot handle dynamic scenes (in-view movers leave artifacts; object relocations invalidate the map).
Cross-modal fusion assumes conditional independence, and failures compound from imperfect modules (rare objects, noisy audio); real-world success is modest (50% on 20 tasks, 6/10 spatial).
